raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`/tag-and-rerun-ci` never starts the sgl-router CI tiers. Seen on #45103 (and #42818 before it): the PR ends up with the `run-ci` label, the "PR Test (sgl-router)" check is green, and every tier job is `skipped`.

Three things in `pr-test-sgl-router.yml` combine to cause it:

1. The gate reads `github.event.pull_request.labels`, a payload frozen when the run was triggered. A rerun replays that payload, so a rerun after the label was added skips again.
2. The slash handler adds `run-ci` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub fires no `labeled` event for such label changes, so no new run starts either.
3. The all-tiers-skipped run concludes `success` (`finish` echoes OK), and the handler only reruns unsuccessful runs, so the hollow run is never rerun at all.

The only ways to get the tiers running were a human removing and re-adding the label by hand, or pushing another commit.

## Modifications

Port the pattern `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-sgl-processor.yml` already use:

- Split path detection into a `changes` job that only answers "does this PR touch sgl-router?".
- Call the shared `pr-gate.yml` for the `run-ci` label. It fetches the labels live and **fails** the gate when the label is missing, instead of skipping. The run is then red, `/tag-and-rerun-ci` reruns it, and the rerun sees the label. `push` to main and `workflow_dispatch` pass straight through as before.
- `finish` checks each tier's result explicitly: success when all tiers passed, or when no router path changed and all tiers were skipped; failure otherwise.

Behavior change for router PRs without `run-ci`: the `gate / pr-gate` and `finish` checks are red rather than green-with-everything-skipped, matching what `call-gate / pr-gate` already does for the Python test workflows.

The `gate` check is now reported as `gate / pr-gate` (reusable-workflow naming, same as `call-gate / pr-gate`). `finish` keeps its name.

## Verification

- `actionlint` on the new file reports only the pre-existing unknown self-hosted label `2-gpu-h100`, identical to main.
- Evidence the rerun path works with the shared gate: pr-test run 39407165818 had `pr-gate` fail on attempt 1 for a missing label and pass on attempt 2 after the label was added, with the test jobs then running.
- This PR touches the workflow file itself, so its own "PR Test (sgl-router)" run exercises the new gate: red without the label, then `/tag-and-rerun-ci` should start tier-1 through tier-3.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci).
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy).
- [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging.
- [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss your PR.

End-to-end check on this PR's own router workflow run (39419134902):

- Attempt 1, no `run-ci` label: `changes` passed, `gate / pr-gate` failed, every tier skipped, `finish` failed, run concluded **failure**.
- Posted `/tag-and-rerun-ci`. The handler log shows `Processing failure workflow: PR Test (sgl-router) ... rerun_failed_jobs`, which it could not do before because the hollow run was green.
- Attempt 2: `gate / pr-gate` passed on the live label set and the tiers started.

For comparison, on #45103 the same slash command left the router run green with every tier skipped, and only removing and re-adding the label by hand got the tiers running.

@@ -6,10 +6,10 @@ name: PR Test (sgl-router)
 #     fires on every PR synchronize / push, so the run record always
 #     appears as a check on the PR (no more "workflow silently didn't
 #     fire" mystery debugging). Path-based skip decisions are made
-#     inside the `sgl-router-gate` job below, where we can log the
+#     inside the `sgl-router-changes` job below, where we can log the
 #     reason. Same for the `run-ci` label gate — moved off the
 #     workflow trigger and into the gate job so its outcome is
-#     observable.
+#     observable, and now fails (rather than skips) when it is missing.
 #
 #   * `push` on `main` keeps firing so post-merge runs still record
 #     against the default branch.
@@ -29,21 +29,17 @@ env:
   SGLANG_IS_IN_CI: true
 
 jobs:
-  # Stage 0 — decide whether to run the heavy tiers. Always runs
-  # (cheap, ubuntu-latest), and emits a single `should_run` output
-  # consumed by every tier below. Reasons it might evict downstream
-  # work:
-  #   * `pull_request` event without the `run-ci` label (budget gate)
-  #   * No files matching the sgl-router paths changed in this PR
-  # Either outcome is logged on the gate job's page, so operators can
-  # see *why* the tiers were skipped instead of guessing.
-  sgl-router-gate:
-    name: gate
+  # Stage 0a — path detection. Always runs (cheap, ubuntu-latest) and
+  # emits a single `should_run` output consumed by every tier below.
+  # It only answers "does this PR touch sgl-router?"; the `run-ci`
+  # label is checked by the separate gate job so that a missing label
+  # fails that job instead of silently skipping the tiers (see below).
+  sgl-router-changes:
+    name: changes
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
     outputs:
       should_run: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.should_run }}
-      paths_changed: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.sgl_router }}
-      has_run_ci_label: ${{ steps.label.outputs.has_run_ci }}
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       # `dorny/paths-filter` computes the diff against the PR base
@@ -53,6 +49,7 @@ jobs:
       # the gate is observable.
       - name: Detect sgl-router path changes
         id: paths
+        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'
         uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
         with:
           filters: |
@@ -64,42 +61,49 @@ jobs:
               - 'proto/**'
               - '.github/workflows/pr-test-sgl-router.yml'
               - 'scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh'
-      # `run-ci` label gate. Cheap workflow runs (e.g. docs-only PRs
-      # that happen to touch the sgl-router dir) still need the
-      # opt-in label before consuming the H100 / kind tiers below.
-      # `push` events on main and `workflow_dispatch` skip this gate.
-      - name: Check run-ci label
-        id: label
-        run: |
-          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]]; then
-            echo "has_run_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
-            echo "Non-PR event (${{ github.event_name }}); label gate bypassed."
-            exit 0
-          fi
-          if [[ "${{ contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'run-ci') }}" == "true" ]]; then
-            echo "has_run_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
-            echo "PR has run-ci label; downstream tiers will run."
-          else
-            echo "has_run_ci=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
-            echo "::warning::PR is missing the 'run-ci' label; skipping sgl-router tiers. Apply the label to opt in."
-          fi
       - name: Decide
         id: decide
+        env:
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+          PATHS_CHANGED: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.sgl_router }}
         run: |
-          paths='${{ steps.paths.outputs.sgl_router }}'
-          label='${{ steps.label.outputs.has_run_ci }}'
-          if [[ "$paths" == "true" && "$label" == "true" ]]; then
+          if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
             echo "should_run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
-            echo "Both path filter and run-ci label match; running tiers."
-          else
+            echo "Manual dispatch; running sgl-router tiers."
+          elif [[ "$PATHS_CHANGED" != "true" ]]; then
             echo "should_run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
-            echo "Skipping tiers (paths_changed=$paths, has_run_ci=$label)."
+            echo "No sgl-router-related changes; skipping tiers."
+          else
+            echo "should_run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            echo "sgl-router-related changes detected; running tiers."
           fi
 
+  # Stage 0b — `run-ci` label gate, shared with `pr-test.yml`. Cheap
+  # workflow runs (e.g. docs-only PRs that happen to touch the
+  # sgl-router dir) still need the opt-in label before consuming the
+  # H100 / kind tiers below. `push` on main and `workflow_dispatch`
+  # pass straight through.
+  #
+  # `pr-gate.yml` fetches the PR's labels live and FAILS when `run-ci`
+  # is missing. Both matter for `/tag-and-rerun-ci`: the slash handler
+  # adds the label with GITHUB_TOKEN, which fires no `labeled` event,
+  # then reruns the PR's unsuccessful runs. A rerun replays the original
+  # event payload, so a gate reading `github.event.pull_request.labels`
+  # would skip again, and a run that concluded `success` with every
+  # tier skipped is never rerun at all. Failing here on the live label
+  # set makes the rerun both happen and pick the label up.
+  sgl-router-gate:
+    name: gate
+    needs: sgl-router-changes
+    if: needs.sgl-router-changes.outputs.should_run == 'true'
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml
+    with:
+      require-run-ci: true
+
   sgl-router-lint:
     name: tier-1 — lint
-    needs: sgl-router-gate
-    if: needs.sgl-router-gate.outputs.should_run == 'true'
+    needs: [sgl-router-changes, sgl-router-gate]
+    if: needs.sgl-router-changes.outputs.should_run == 'true'
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     env:
       # Scoped per-job (not workflow-wide) to avoid SMG's documented breakage
@@ -167,8 +171,8 @@ jobs:
 
   sgl-router-build-and-test:
     name: tier-2 — build + test
-    needs: [sgl-router-gate, sgl-router-lint]
-    if: needs.sgl-router-gate.outputs.should_run == 'true'
+    needs: [sgl-router-changes, sgl-router-gate, sgl-router-lint]
+    if: needs.sgl-router-changes.outputs.should_run == 'true'
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     env:
       RUSTC_WRAPPER: sccache
@@ -268,8 +272,8 @@ jobs:
 
   sgl-router-docker-build-test:
     name: tier-3 — docker (placeholder)
-    needs: [sgl-router-gate, sgl-router-build-and-test]
-    if: needs.sgl-router-gate.outputs.should_run == 'true'
+    needs: [sgl-router-changes, sgl-router-gate, sgl-router-build-and-test]
+    if: needs.sgl-router-changes.outputs.should_run == 'true'
     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
     timeout-minutes: 15
     steps:
@@ -286,8 +290,8 @@ jobs:
   # the GPU/cluster runners from spinning up.
   sgl-router-k8s-integration:
     name: tier-3 — k8s integration
-    needs: [sgl-router-gate, sgl-router-build-and-test]
-    if: needs.sgl-router-gate.outputs.should_run == 'true'
+    needs: [sgl-router-changes, sgl-router-gate, sgl-router-build-and-test]
+    if: needs.sgl-router-changes.outputs.should_run == 'true'
     runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
     timeout-minutes: 30
     steps:
@@ -333,8 +337,8 @@ jobs:
 
   sgl-router-e2e:
     name: tier-3 — e2e
-    needs: [sgl-router-gate, sgl-router-build-and-test]
-    if: needs.sgl-router-gate.outputs.should_run == 'true'
+    needs: [sgl-router-changes, sgl-router-gate, sgl-router-build-and-test]
+    if: needs.sgl-router-changes.outputs.should_run == 'true'
     runs-on: 2-gpu-h100
     timeout-minutes: 45
     steps:
@@ -394,25 +398,43 @@ jobs:
   sgl-router-finish:
     name: finish
     needs:
+      - sgl-router-changes
       - sgl-router-gate
       - sgl-router-lint
       - sgl-router-build-and-test
       - sgl-router-docker-build-test
       - sgl-router-k8s-integration
       - sgl-router-e2e
-    # `always()` lets `finish` run after upstream `skipped` outcomes
-    # (when the gate decided to skip). The downstream-skipped path is
-    # an explicit success — the workflow was correctly bypassed for a
-    # PR that didn't need full CI. The downstream-failure /
-    # downstream-cancelled path is a real fail. We also accept the
-    # gate's `skipped` (impossible today, kept for symmetry) and
-    # require the gate itself to have succeeded.
-    if: |
-      always() &&
-      needs.sgl-router-gate.result == 'success' &&
-      !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&
-      !contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')
+    # `always()` lets `finish` run after upstream `skipped` outcomes.
+    # Two outcomes are a success: every tier passed, or the PR touches
+    # no sgl-router path and every tier was skipped. Anything else,
+    # including a gate that failed for a missing `run-ci` label, fails
+    # the run, so `/tag-and-rerun-ci` sees an unsuccessful run to rerun.
+    if: always()
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
     steps:
-      - name: All required checks completed
-        run: echo "OK"
+      - name: Check required results
+        env:
+          CHANGES_RESULT: ${{ needs.sgl-router-changes.result }}
+          SHOULD_RUN: ${{ needs.sgl-router-changes.outputs.should_run }}
+          GATE_RESULT: ${{ needs.sgl-router-gate.result }}
+          LINT_RESULT: ${{ needs.sgl-router-lint.result }}
+          BUILD_RESULT: ${{ needs.sgl-router-build-and-test.result }}
+          DOCKER_RESULT: ${{ needs.sgl-router-docker-build-test.result }}
+          K8S_RESULT: ${{ needs.sgl-router-k8s-integration.result }}
+          E2E_RESULT: ${{ needs.sgl-router-e2e.result }}
+        run: |
+          if [[ "$CHANGES_RESULT" != "success" ]]; then
+            echo "::error::sgl-router path detection did not succeed ($CHANGES_RESULT)."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          tiers="$GATE_RESULT $LINT_RESULT $BUILD_RESULT $DOCKER_RESULT $K8S_RESULT $E2E_RESULT"
+          if [[ "$SHOULD_RUN" == "true" && "$tiers" == "success success success success success success" ]]; then
+            echo "All sgl-router checks passed."
+          elif [[ "$SHOULD_RUN" == "false" && "$tiers" == "skipped skipped skipped skipped skipped skipped" ]]; then
+            echo "No sgl-router-related changes; tiers skipped."
+          else
+            echo "::error::Unexpected sgl-router results: should_run=$SHOULD_RUN, gate=$GATE_RESULT, lint=$LINT_RESULT, build=$BUILD_RESULT, docker=$DOCKER_RESULT, k8s=$K8S_RESULT, e2e=$E2E_RESULT."
+            exit 1
+          fi
